name: Apali
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Daniels, Don Roger 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram (UCSB dissertation; Apali/Apalɨ phonology pp. 84-85); also SIL materials by Martha Wade (Apalɨ grammar essentials).
earlier_scan.note: Daniels 2015 PDF (alexandria.ucsb.edu) could not be reached by automated download; SIL resource search 403; Wikipedia Apali cites Daniels for vowels only, no stress statement.

sources.citation: Wade, Martha. 1993. Language convergence or divergence: The case of the Apali (Emerum) language. Language and Linguistics in Melanesia 24: 73-93.
sources.note: Section 3 'Phonological differences' (pp. 75-81) covers the phoneme inventory (Table 1), allophones, dialect correspondences, phoneme frequencies and vowels; the words stress, accent, tone do not occur anywhere in the article (scanned of a 600-dpi image scan, rendered at 300 dpi).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Southern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-33. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Contains the Emerum (H3) wordlist; the introduction has no note on stress; the only prosodic remark is that Isabi and Biyom are the only tonal languages known in the Adelbert Range group (p. vi).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J.A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Emerum (= Apalɨ) appears only in the classification tables and village list (pp. 14-25, 69-76); the strings 'stress'/'accent' do not occur in the volume's text.

sources.citation: Rosetta Project. n.d. Apali Swadesh List (archive.org rosettaproject_ena_swadesh-1).
sources.note: Bare wordlist in two transcriptions; no stress marks, no notes.

sources.citation: OLAC combined catalog, resources in and about the Apali language (Internet Archive copy 2025-02-10).
sources.note: Lists Rosetta Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org, Glottolog, PARADISEC field recordings and notebooks (Daniels DD1-230, DD1-682, DD1-957; Pawley AP4), Ethnologue, LINGUIST List, SIL 22818 (Wade 1997). No phonological description listed.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2020. Grammatical Reconstruction: The Sogeram Languages of New Guinea. Trends in Linguistics Studies and Monographs. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: Comparative-historical book version of the dissertation; its introductory chapter on the Sogeram languages and their phonology may add a stress statement per language or for Proto-Sogeram that the 2015 dissertation lacks.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don. 2015. A Reconstruction of Proto-Sogeram: Phonology, Lexicon, and Morphosyntax. PhD dissertation, University of California, Santa Barbara. 1126 pp.
sources.note: §2.3.3 'Apalɨ Innovations' (pp. 84-91) gives the Apalɨ phoneme inventory and sound changes but says nothing about stress. 'Stress' occurs only twice in the whole dissertation: p. 72 (Mand section) 'Further research into the stress systems of the Sogeram languages might reveal a consistent pattern', and p. 338 'commonly stressed word classes' (Western Sogeram final *a loss). No Apalɨ grammar sketch is included; Wade's manuscripts are cited instead (Wade 1987 phonological analysis, Wade 1989 grammar survey).

sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives, search results for language ena (Internet Archive copy 2015-09-22).
sources.note: Only one archived item for Apalɨ: Wade 'Switch reference and control in Apalɨ' (sil.org/resources/archives/22818). No Organised Phonology Data or phonology write-up for Apalɨ in the SIL archive. Live sil.org returns an automated-access block could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: Daniels, Don R. 2010. A preliminary phonological history of the Sogeram languages of Papua New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 49(1): 163-193.
sources.note: Glottolog's 'phonology' entry for Apalɨ; the phoneme-inventory descriptions of each Sogeram language could mention stress, though the 2015 dissertation that supersedes it does not.

sources.citation: Wade, Martha. 1997. Switch reference and control in Apalɨ. Language and Linguistics in Melanesia 28: 1-16.
sources.note: Syntax paper (switch reference); no phonology section, nothing on stress.
Vowel table only, citing Daniels 2015 pp. 84-85; nothing on stress. Supplied the ADRL download id (2r36tx861) for the dissertation.
